conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you so much for making time for this today. I’m Dr. Bennett, a perinatal-mental-health clinician, and I’ll be guiding you through a brief screening we do with every new parent. The tool we’ll use is called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply a set of 10 questions that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve.

Everything we discuss stays confidential within the care team unless you tell me something that makes me worry about your immediate safety or your baby’s safety—then we’d talk together about the next steps. There are no right or wrong answers, and many new parents find some of the questions surprisingly relatable. We’ll go one question at a time; each one is short and asks about mood, anxiety, and coping. If at any point you need a break, just let me know.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

*shifts in chair, eyes downcast*

Not really... I mean, I can smile when my husband tries to be funny, but it's not the same. Before the baby, I used to laugh all the time, but now... everything just feels kind of heavy. Even when I watch something funny on TV, it's like I can't quite get there.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

*shakes head slowly*

No… not really. I can smile sometimes, but even when my partner makes a joke I used to find hilarious, it just falls flat for me now. I *want* to laugh, but it’s like something’s blocking it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

*shrugs, voice quiet*

Not much anymore. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet evening. Now… I *try* to look forward to stuff, but it feels kind of dull, like what’s the point? I still go, but the spark isn’t really there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

*nods, eyes welling up*

Yeah… a lot. If the baby cries for more than a few minutes, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—maybe I’m not feeding him right, or I missed some cue. Yesterday I spilled a little pumped milk and I sat on the kitchen floor crying because I felt like I’d failed him. I *know* logically it’s not a big deal, but the guilt just crashes over me.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

*twists the edge of the blanket in my lap*

Yes… pretty much every day. I’ll be rocking the baby and suddenly my heart starts racing because I’m sure he’s going to stop breathing, even though he’s fine. Or I’ll lie down and think the ceiling fan is going to fall on him. I *know* it’s unlikely, but I can’t switch the thoughts off. Sometimes I have to get up and check him three or four times before I can settle.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

*presses a hand to chest*

A couple of times, yeah. It’s like a sudden wave—my heart starts pounding and I feel I can’t catch my breath. Nothing’s happening, but my body acts like the house is on fire. It passes after a minute or two, but it leaves me shaky and on-edge the rest of the day.
Things have been getting on top of me

*nods slowly, exhaling*

Yes… most days. Between feeding, changing, trying to sleep, and then the house being a mess, it feels like I’m drowning in small stuff. Some mornings I just stare at the pile of laundry and want to cry because I don’t know where to start. I manage, but it’s like I’m barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

*pulls cardigan tighter*

Yes… several nights this week. I’ll finally get the baby down, but then I lie there with my mind racing—going over everything I might have done wrong, worrying something bad will happen. It takes me an hour or more to fall asleep, and when I do drift off, I wake up again with a jolt of anxiety. I’m exhausted, but my brain just won’t settle.
I have felt sad or miserable

*eyes glaze, voice cracks*

Yeah… pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly feel like crying for no real reason. Yesterday I just sat in the rocker staring at the wall, feeling empty. I keep telling myself I should be happy—he’s healthy, I’m lucky—but the sadness just sits there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

*voice drops to a whisper, dabbing at eyes with sleeve*

Yes… twice this week. Once was after I couldn’t soothe him for almost an hour—I finally put him down in the crib safe, went to the bathroom, and just sobbed into a towel. The other time was when my mom called to check in; I couldn’t even finish the sentence “I’m okay” before the tears started. It feels like the sadness just spills out whether I want it to or not.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

*hesitates, looks away*

Once or twice… just fleeting, like a quick flash—“what if I wasn’t here?” I haven’t made any plans or anything like that, and I don’t want to leave my baby, but when I’m really overwhelmed the thought pops in for a second and then I feel awful for even thinking it.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms endorsed  
- Marked anhedonia (Q1, Q2)  
- Daily low mood, frequent crying spells (Q8, Q9)  
- Pathologic guilt / self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)  
- Persistent, intrusive anxiety and panic without clear trigger (Q4, Q5)  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed and unable to cope (Q6)  
- Mood-congruent insomnia (difficulty initiating / maintaining sleep) (Q7)  
- Fleeting passive self-harm ideation without plan or intent (Q10)  

Pattern  
Consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; functional impact evident in sleep, emotional regulation, and caregiving confidence.

Risk flags  
- Passive SI (safety concern)  
- Significant guilt / worthlessness  
- Anxiety manifesting as panic attacks and excessive infant safety checking  

Screening impression  
High clinical likelihood of postpartum depression ± anxiety; safety risk present. Referral for urgent psychiatric evaluation and safety planning recommended.
